# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Iowa Total Care — Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Reese Carter
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18**
- **Member:** Reese Carter
- **Member ID:** W451155739
- **Reference number:** POC-EF30A43966-84895
- **Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
- **Plan:** Iowa Total Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Iowa
- **Governing policy:** *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines*, effective 2026-07-01 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which Iowa Total Care denied on 2026-08-18. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure, because my records do document a lengthy and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, submitted a prior authorization packet documenting that this surgery is needed.

## The plan's own definition of failed conservative treatment

The *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines* define what it means for conservative treatment to have failed. The guidelines state:

> "NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:"

> "○ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;"

> "OR ○ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment;"

The guidelines also make clear what does **not** count as a failure to complete treatment:

> "OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

That last point matters here, because nothing of the kind happened in my case. I did not skip treatment, cut it short, or decline to participate. I completed it.

## How my records meet that standard

**The plan's standard: "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment."**
My records show a full course of treatment, completed:

- **Supervised physical therapy:** 14 weeks, from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20, with 18 visits completed, focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-27, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief.

After all of that, I still cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and I cannot sleep on the affected side. On examination, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. That is a lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment, in the plan's own words.

**The plan's standard: "Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment."**
My symptom history is 12 months of *progressive* pain in the shoulder, unrelieved by rest. Imaging on 2026-07-07 — an MRI of the shoulder obtained after my physical therapy was underway — showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.

**I am also an appropriate surgical candidate on the general safety factors in my chart:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and I am a non-smoker.

So on the single issue the denial raises — conservative care — the records already in the plan's possession match the plan's own definition of failed conservative treatment, on both of the first two alternatives, and none of the excluded reasons (office closure, inconvenience, unexplained noncompliance) applies to me.

## A note about the criteria I was given, in fairness to the reviewer

I want to be straightforward about one thing. The criteria excerpts available to me from the *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines* are drawn from the cervical spine sections of that document — anterior cervical discectomy with fusion, cervical posterior decompression with fusion, and cervical fusion for axial neck pain. For example, the guidelines state:

> "● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;"

I have a shoulder condition, not a cervical spine condition, and the procedure requested is a total shoulder replacement. I have **not** been quoted the shoulder arthroplasty criteria that were actually applied to my request, so I cannot map my records to them line by line. What I can show is that the conservative-care requirement quoted above — a minimum of six weeks of conservative treatment within the last six months — is far exceeded by my 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20, 4 months of NSAIDs, and an injection on 2026-05-27, all within the six months before the request.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

I am asking Iowa Total Care to send me, in writing and at no cost, the complete clinical criteria that were actually used to deny CPT 23472 in my case — the specific section and the specific requirement my records were found not to meet. I understand that Iowa Total Care routes shoulder, hip, spine, and knee surgery requests to Evolent, and that Evolent's criteria are published on RadMD at no charge. If my request was reviewed under the *2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines*, please identify the section applied so that I can respond to it directly. The plan holds the criteria it applied; I am asking the plan to provide them.

## Closing request

I am asking Iowa Total Care to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 (reference POC-EF30A43966-84895) and approve the total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472, requested by Dr. Marchetti. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise, and that the physical therapy discharge note, the 2026-07-07 MRI report, and Dr. Marchetti's operative request be reviewed as part of the file.

Per the notice I received, this appeal must be received by **2027-02-14** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file using my state's appeal form at ambetterhealth.com or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please send your decision in writing to the address above. If any additional records would help, please tell me what is missing and I will ask my surgeon's office to send it.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Reese Carter**
Member ID: W451155739
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-18] · [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20] · [MRI report, 2026-07-07] · [Office notes from Dr. Marchetti] · [Medication and injection records]
